'''Raúl Gonzalo Cuero Rengifo''' (born 1948 in [[Buenaventura, Valle del Cauca|Buenaventura]], [[Colombia]]) is a [[Colombians|Colombian]] professor of microbiology.  From 1988 through 2012 he was a professor at [[Prairie View A&M University]] researching biological resistance to [[ultraviolet]] light.<ref name=Quest/><ref name="CV">
{{cite web |url=http://www.raulcuerobiotech.com/about/professional_experiences.html |title=Professional Experiences |last=Cuero |first=Raúl |work=RaulCueroBiotech.com |accessdate=14 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131127015731/http://raulcuerobiotech.com/about/professional_experiences.html |archive-date=27 November 2013 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}
</ref>  The work was supported in part by [[NASA]] and led to at least one publication and patent.  During this period, Colombian media portrayed Cuero as "one of the greatest scientists in the world"<ref name=ElPais/> who was internationally acknowledged as one of the greatest Colombian inventors,<ref name=ElColombiano2/> stated he had over 100 publications in scientific journals,<ref name=ElColombiano/> and claimed he had won a significant award from NASA.<ref name=ElUniversal/> Since 2012, he has been the research director of International Park of Creativity, an organization of which he is the founder.<ref name="CV"/>
